evidence.title: Every heap climbing
evidence.body: Checkout heap averages 78% on all twelve instances, up from 49% ten minutes ago. GC pauses reach 880 ms.

evidence.title: Checkout handler log
evidence.body: Every checkout logs "response sent" and then, minutes later, its request object is still being walked by the garbage collector. Nothing is being let go.

evidence.title: Completed requests held by their callbacks
evidence.body: Heap dump: checkout-handler / completionCallbacks / completed-request. 1.9 million requests kept alive after their responses were sent.

evidence.title: Sam's heap snapshots
evidence.body: Completed requests pile up under completionCallbacks. A restart empties the pile and it refills at the same slope. Rolling back to 4.11 brings back the large-cart crash.

evidence.title: Tonight's big carts
evidence.body: 6% of tonight's carts have more than 50 items, almost all of them wholesale reorders.

evidence.title: Release 4.12 never lets go
evidence.body: 4.12 registers a completion callback per request behind checkout.completion_callbacks and never removes it. 4.11 has no callback, and still has the large-cart crash 4.12 fixed.

evidence.title: Deleted allocation log fragment
evidence.body: UNKNOWN: the objects are gone. the references are not.

beats.narrate: An evening shift, for once. The storefront has been counting down to the evening sale all afternoon.

beats.speaker: PAGER
beats.text: SEV2 · Checkout API · heap above 75% on 3 or more instances

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Checkout heap is climbing on every instance, not just one. The evening sale opens in about four minutes. I want this understood before then.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: A handful of customers say the payment screen spins and never finishes. Not many yet.

beats.speaker: ADVISOR
beats.text: Recommended action: scale checkout pool from 12 to 20 instances. Projected heap per instance: 61%. Confidence 0.88.

beats.narrate: Your ticket about the redacted request came back this afternoon. "Redaction performed by system account." It doesn't say which one.
The timestamp from before batch 781 is still on a sticky note under your monitor. Nobody has claimed that request.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: About the marker. I asked around without asking. Nobody admits redacting anything. Keep it off the tickets.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I'm on the bridge. Hand me whatever you don't want to do yourself.

options.text: Read the handler log, then take a heap dump

beats.log: heap dump checkout-07: completionCallbacks → CompletedCheckoutRequest ×1,903,227 · 2.31 GB

beats.narrate: Nearly two million checkouts that finished long ago, each one still held by the callback that fired when it did.
The last row of the dump is a single 4 KB block. Its owner is listed as a deleted process. Later.

options.text: Ask Sam to compare two heap snapshots
options.consequence: A minute and a half · Sam owns that part

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: On it. Two heap snapshots a minute apart will tell us what's growing.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: GC is running back to back on checkout-07. Pauses are at 900 ms and climbing.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Snapshots agree. Completed requests pile up under completionCallbacks. A restart empties the pile and it refills at the same slope. And please don't roll back to 4.11. That's the release that crashes on big carts.

options.text: Ask Jin who is actually failing
options.consequence: Slower · you'll know who gets hurt

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Spinners everywhere, no pattern by region. One thing — six percent of tonight's carts are wholesale reorders, fifty items and up. Those customers call.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Took a heap dump while you two talked. 1.9 million finished checkouts, all held under completionCallbacks.

beats.narrate: The release diff loads. Last week's 4.11 on the left, tonight's 4.12 on the right.

beats.log: 4.12 (today 18:40): completion callbacks one per request · flag checkout.completion_callbacks = on
4.12: callback removal not implemented (ticket CHK-2207, open)
4.11: carts over 50 items crash at pricing (CHK-2181) · fixed in 4.12

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Tonight's release registers a callback for every checkout and never takes it back. And the release before it can't price a big cart.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The callbacks sit behind a flag. Turning it off is a redeploy. Ninety seconds.

scenes.title: Your call

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: The sale opens in a minute. Support still has nothing to tell anyone.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Support can't keep up. The same failure keeps coming in from every channel.

scenes.prompt: What do you do about the leak?

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: No call? I'm taking the advisor's eight instances. It's a number, at least.

options.text: Turn off the completion-callback flag on tonight's release
options.consequence: Ninety seconds of redeploy · the sale opens halfway through

beats.narrate: The sale opens halfway through the redeploy. For thirty seconds, checkouts stall on the instances still waiting their turn.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Flag is off. The callback registry drained on the next collection and heap is flat at 39%. Big carts are pricing fine.

options.text: Restart the checkout instances to empty the heap
options.consequence: Fast · the same handler fills them again

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Rolling restart finished. Heap is down to 41% on every instance. Same build, same handler.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: The evening sale is live. Traffic doubled, and so did the complaints.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: With the sale running, the restarted instances filled up in just over a minute.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: checkout-03 and checkout-09 just got killed for running out of memory. Every cart in flight on them is gone.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Enough. Turn the callbacks off.

options.text: Roll checkout back to last week's release (4.11)
options.consequence: Stops the leak · brings back last week's bug

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: 4.11 is live and the heap is flat. And every cart over fifty items is crashing at pricing again. That's the bug 4.12 was shipped to fix.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Our wholesale accounts can't place orders. Anything over fifty lines dies at pricing. Those are our biggest customers.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Roll forward. 4.12, flag off.

beats.narrate: For two minutes the advisor's number holds. Then the new instances start to look like the old ones.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: All twenty instances are leaking now. We nearly doubled the bill and bought two minutes.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Turn the callbacks off. Then scale us back down.

beats.narrate: The heap is quiet. Sam takes one last dump to close the incident, and one row refuses to drain.

beats.log: completionCallbacks · (unnamed block) · 1 · 4 KB · owner pid 3318 (process deleted)

beats.narrate: You look up pid 3318. The scheduler says it ran for two minutes, nine days ago, from an image with no deploy record. Then its entry was deleted.

beats.log: 9 days ago 03:15 · cold log store · pid 3318: UNKNOWN: the objects are gone. the references are not.

beats.narrate: The line was written a minute after the process stopped existing.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I checked pid 3318 three times. It was deleted nine days ago. I don't know how a process that doesn't exist is holding memory in tonight's build.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Write down the date. I want to know what else happened that night.

scenes.title: Postmortem

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The leak writes itself. What about the block?

scenes.prompt: What do you do with pid 3318?

options.text: Put pid 3318 and the cold-store line in the postmortem
options.consequence: On the record · Security will read it

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Then it's on the record. Good luck finding an owner for a process that doesn't exist.

options.text: Ask Sam to quietly pull everything pid 3318 ever touched
options.consequence: Off the books · Sam's name on it too

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Quietly. Sure. Give me a few days.

options.text: Report the leak only; copy the cold-store line for yourself
options.consequence: A clean report · the line stays yours
